description.narrative:
Insatsen avser ett obundet organisationsstöd till United Nations Volunteers Programme genom Special Voluntary Fund (SVF). Stödet bidrar till genomförandet av den verksamhet som finns representerad i UNV:s strategiska ramverk för perioden 2022-2025, samt tillhörade resultatmatris.
UNV:s strategiska ramverk för perioden 2022-2025 bygger på lärdomar från den tidigare strategiperioden. Den avser att främja volontärismen som ett kraftfullt sätt att bidra till genomförandet av Agenda 2030 för hållbar utveckling. Den ser även volontärismen som ett verktyg för att engagera FNs utvecklingssystem, medlemsstater, det civila samhället och den privata sektorn. För detta ändamål har UNV identifierat tre resultatområden:
1. Contributing to a people-centred United Nations: The functioning of the United Nations system is supported through the engagement of empowered UN Volunteers;
2. Serving the United Nations system: UNV is a fit-for-purpose organization contributing to the efficiency gains of the United Nations system; and
3. Promote volunteerism: Efforts by Member States and the United Nations system to integrate volunteerism into the 2030 Agenda as a cross-cutting means of implementation are supported.
UNVs strategiska ramverk är nära länkat till generalförsamlingens resolution 75/233 antaget den 21 december 2020 Quadrennial Comprehensive Policy Review (QCPR). Den vägleds även av av generalförsamlingen resolutioner 70/129 från den 15 december 2015 om integrating volunteering into peace and development: the plan of action for the next decade and beyon och 73/140 av den 17 december 2018 om "volunteering for the 2030 Agenda for sustainable development".
Obundet organisationsstöd till United Nations Volunteers (UNV) för genomförande av UNVs strategiska ramverk för perioden 2022-2025 genom Special Voluntary Fund, perioden 2022-2023.
Untied organizational support to United Nations Volunteers (UNV) for the implementation of UNV's strategic framework for the period 2022-2025 through the Special Voluntary Fund, period 2022-2023.

In 2023, the SVF funds were used to support UNV in responding to critical emergencies and crises, promoting volunteerism through inclusion and diversity with increased assignments of national UN volunteers with disability and from underrepresented small developing states with six SVF funded UN volunteers sent to support the capacity of the UN Multi-Contry Office in Micronesia. In 2023, UNV mobilized 12 840 UN volunteers with 88% from Global South countries. 64% of all UN volounteers 2023, served as national volounteers, while 36% where international UN Volunteers. UN Volunteers also contributed to the UN systemwide action plans on gender equality and inclusion, integration of Agenda 2030 into UN programme operation and national development. Out of 12 840 volunteers 36% report that they contributed to Sustainabale Development Goal (SDG) 16. Volunteers also report that they contributed to SDG 5 (20%), SDG 3 (19%) and SDG 17 (19%).
The majority of UN volunteers served in Africa (5299 volunteers). Latin America and the Caribbean (2762) is the second largest contigent, followed by Asia and the Pacific (1931 volunteers), The Arab States region (1649 volunteers) and lastly the Europe and the Commonwealth of Independent States (1224 volunteers).
UNV results and achivements from 2023 include:
- 57% of UN volunteers are female, which is a 2% growth from 2022. Notable is the gender balance among UNV personal, which has resulted in sustaining strong performance under the UN System-wide Action Plan on Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women. Additonal mentionable results is the commitment to South-South cooperation. Out of the 11339 UN volunteers from Global South countries, 8027 served as national UN volunteers in their countries of origin. The remaining 3350 UN volunteers from Global South countries served as international volunteers in other Global South nations.
- Promoting inclusion and diversity has continued to be an important focus area for UNV. In 2023, 187 UN volunteers with disabilities served with 27 UN entities. In total Sweden has funded 82 UN volunteers with disabilities, with 79 of 82 from partner countries.
- Another major result is the UNV contribution to humanitarian crises such as the war in Ukraine and crises in Gaza trough funding UN volunteers to support member states and UN agencies. At the end of 2023, 18 SVF-funded UN volunteers were recruited or were under recruitment with 6 UN entities to support the Gaza crisis response. In response of the war in Ukraine, UNV deployed 12 SVF-funded UN volunteers at partner entities.
- Post emergency assistance has remained a priority, with UN volunteers contributing to the relief efforts following the earthquake in Morocco. In the context of the crises in Afghanistan, the SVF enabled UNV to continue reassigning Afghan UN volunteers abroad. In 2022, the SVF funds were used to support UNV in responding to critical emergencies and crises, promoting volunteerism through inclusion and diversity with increased assignments of national UN volunteers with disability and from non-and underrepresented small developing states, as well as increased female volunteers to all UN agencies and programmes across the world. UN Volunteers also contributed to the UN system-wide action plans on gender equality and inclusion, integration of Agenda 2030 into UN programme operation and national development.
In 2022, 12,408 UN Volunteers from 179 nationalities were deployed, representing an increase of 14 per cent over 2021, to support 55 UN partners in 166 countries and territories. 84% of the total UN Volunteers deployed were from the global south, of those 70% served as national UN Volunteers and contributed to the peace and development of their own countries. Based on the data from 9,738 volunteer reports found that onethird of volunteers contributed to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 16 (38%). Significant numbers of volunteers also contributed to SDG 3 (20%), SDG 5 (20%) and SDG 10 (15%). The largest number of UN Volunteers served in Africa. Latin America and the Caribbean is the next largest contingent, followed by Asia and the Pacific. The Arab States region was next, followed by Europe and the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
During 2022, the most important results UNV achieved are:
- UNV gained major steps toward gender quality with the proportion of women UN Volunteers increased to 55 per cent. Particularly, the increase in the number of women volunteers from Africa, where 48 per cent of UN Volunteers on the continent were women a marked increase from 40 per cent in 2018. UNV partnered with UN peacekeeping missions to increase the number of women UN Volunteers among civilian personnel. As a result, women made up 42 per cent of UN Volunteers in peacekeeping in 2022, compared to 39 per cent in 2021 and 32 per cent in 2017. UNV as organization also made a strong contribution to the UN system-wide action plan on gender equality and the empowerment of women it achieved gender balance across levels of staff.
- Promoting inclusion and diversity through UN system volunteerism gained a strong momentum. A great number of national and international UN Volunteers with disabilities have been deployed in 2022, accounting for 12% of all assigned volunteers. UNV recruited and trained 205 UN Volunteers with disabilities and connected them with 23 UN entities. Contribution from Germany and Sweden to the SVF to fund volunteer assignments for persons with disabilities from programme countries resulted in 42 new deployments in 2022. UNV also put further focus for increasing the number of UN Volunteers from non and underrepresented small island developing States in the Caribbean and North Pacific. UNV itself exceeded the target on staff coming from the global south, representing 64%.
- Another major result UNV contributed in 2022 was extra efforts and deployments of UN Volunteers in responding to critical emergencies and crises such as the floodings in Pakistan, earthquakes in Haiti, the crisis in Afghanistan and the war in Ukraine. Through the SVF funds, UNV took targeted and immediate action by funding UN Volunteers to support member states and UN entities in numerous forms of assistance. In response to the war in Ukraine, UNV used the SVF to fund 16 UN Volunteer assignments at partner entities in 2022. In total, UNV deployed 284 UN Volunteers to 15 United Nations entities in Ukraine and neighbouring countries. Other examples of post-emergency assistance UN Volunteers contributed to include support during the aftermath of the Haiti earthquake and the floods in Pakistan. In Haiti, UNV used the SVF to fund national UN Volunteers to strengthen the work on the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse. In Pakistan, through the SVF, UNV mobilized UN Volunteers to support response efforts soon after the devastating floods in 2022. In the context of the crisis in Afghanistan, the SVF enabled UNV to continue supporting the redeployment of 11 Afghan UN Volunteers who were moved out of the country in 2021 and have since served in UNV Regional Offices as well as with UN Women.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
